learning.title: Call the installed binary when a mise-wrapped CLI re-execs itself forever
learning.trigger: A CLI such as rig or gh exits 124 under timeout with zero bytes on stdout and stderr, even for --version or --help, while git and curl against the same hosts work.
learning.rule: Check what the shim is before debugging the tool. /home/marktripoli/.local/bin/rig runs "mise exec node@22.22.0 -- rig" and /home/marktripoli/.local/bin/gh runs "mise use -g --quiet gh" first. The measured mechanism is a re-exec loop: the shim resolves the command name back to the shim, so strace during the outage showed 74+ execve cycles of wrapper to mise to wrapper and zero network syscalls, while curl to api.github.com answered in the same shell. Look for the exec loop before looking at connectivity. Workaround either way: call the installed binary directly, ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/22.22.0/bin/rig and ~/.local/share/mise/installs/gh/latest/gh_2.100.0_linux_amd64/bin/gh (confirm the path with ls of the installs dir). A whole seat can look wedged for hours this way while the agent's own reasoning is fine; the give-away is that even --version hangs.

verification.requirement: Prove it with exit codes and syscall evidence, not impressions: the wrapper path times out (124, empty output), the direct binary prints a version and exits 0 in the same shell, and strace of the wrapper shows repeated execve of the shim rather than network syscalls. Record the working absolute path in the handover so the next occupant does not rediscover it.
